title: Middle support and cosupport define a bounded perverse t-structure
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, and let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. In $\mathcal C_T=D^b_c(T,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], use the relative Verdier dual $D_T$ and its normalization from [lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality]. Define the shifted classes ${}^pD^{\le n}(T)$ and ${}^pD^{\ge n}(T)$ by [def-per-support-condition, def-per-perverse-subcategories]: the first is characterized by $\dim\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^j(K)\le n-j$ for all $j$, the second by $D_TK\in{}^pD^{\le -n}(T)$, and the empty support has dimension $-\infty$. This pair is a bounded t-structure in the sense of [def-weil-t-structure]. In particular, for every $n\in\mathbf Z$,
$$K\in{}^pD^{\ge n}(T)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)=0\text{ for every }A\in{}^pD^{\le n-1}(T).$$
The two classes at every index are closed under extensions.

source.place: Sections 2.2.11--2.2.19 and 4.0 (middle perversity); adic categories interpreted by Bhatt--Scholze Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15

proof.text: Write $P^{\le n}_W,P^{\ge n}_W$ for the two classes in the statement, always using the arbitrary-field dual of [lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality], rather than the finite-field dual mentioned by the older support definition. The formulas of [def-per-support-condition, def-per-perverse-subcategories] give $P^{\le n}=P^{\le0}[-n]$. Since $D(K[n])\cong DK[-n]$ and $D^2K\cong K$, they also give $P^{\ge n}=P^{\ge0}[-n]$ and $D(P^{\ge n})=P^{\le -n}$. Increasing an upper index weakens the support inequalities, so $P^{\le n}\subseteq P^{\le n+1}$, and duality gives $P^{\ge n+1}\subseteq P^{\ge n}$. In particular the shift inclusions in the definition of a t-structure hold.

For a complementary pair $j:U\hookrightarrow W$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow W$, we claim $K\in P^{\le n}_W$ if and only if $j^*K\in P^{\le n}_U$ and $i^*K\in P^{\le n}_Z$. By [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres], each cohomology sheaf $F$ has a constructible nonzero-fibre locus $C$, and pullback restricts this locus. Write $C$ as a finite union of locally closed strata, refining by $U,Z$. For each nonempty stratum $S$, the first inequality of [lem-zl-finite-type-fibre-image-dimension-bounds], applied to $S\hookrightarrow W$, gives $\dim\overline S\le\dim S$; the reverse inequality follows by viewing chains in $S$ inside its closure. A finite union of closures has dimension their maximum: an irreducible closed subset of the union lies in one member. Consequently $\dim\overline C=\max(\dim\overline{C\cap U}^{\,U},\dim\overline{C\cap Z}^{\,Z})$, with empty terms $-\infty$. Indeed the same strata compute each side and their dimensions do not change under their locally closed inclusions, by the same inequality and reverse inequality. Apply this equality to every $F=\mathcal H^rK$, using the cohomology identities of [lem-per-qbar-dual-recollement], to prove the claim. In particular supports here may be taken closed, as in [def-per-support-condition].

source.place: 1.4.9 and 4.0.1: the support class is glued by ordinary restrictions

proof.text:
Apply Step 2 to $D_WK$. The identities $j^*D_WK\cong D_Uj^*K$ and $i^*D_WK\cong D_Zi^!K$ from [lem-per-qbar-dual-recollement] give
$$K\in P^{\ge n}_W\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad j^*K\in P^{\ge n}_U\ \text{and}\ i^!K\in P^{\ge n}_Z.$$
This is a direct substitution into the cosupport definition, with index $-n$.

source.place: 1.4.9: the cosupport class is glued by extraordinary closed restriction

proof.text: Use [lem-per-qbar-generic-duality-model] for any finite family of complexes on a nonempty $W$. On each of its irreducible open pieces $V$ of dimension $d$, a nonzero lisse constant-rank sheaf has support all of $V$: its fibres have positive rank everywhere, by the exact conservative fibres of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres]. Thus a lisse-cohomology complex $L$ satisfies $L\in P^{\le n}_V$ exactly when $\mathcal H^aL=0$ for $a>n-d$. The dual formula in [lem-per-qbar-generic-duality-model] says that $\mathcal H^r(D_VL)$ vanishes exactly when $\mathcal H^{-r-2d}L$ does. Applying the upper formula with index $-n$, and substituting $a=-r-2d$, gives $L\in P^{\ge n}_V$ exactly when $\mathcal H^aL=0$ for $a<n-d$. These are ordinary shifted cohomological bounds, with ordinary truncations provided by [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres]. On a finite disjoint union of these pieces, the sum of extension-by-zero maps from the restrictions is an isomorphism: [lem-per-qbar-dual-recollement] defines the maps and their geometric fibres are the identity on the one relevant summand. Conservativity of fibres and bounded cohomology give the isomorphism. Hence the bounds and Hom groups can be checked piece by piece.

source.place: 1.4.10 and 2.2.10--2.2.12: local ordinary bounds and dimension-normalized duality

proof.text: We prove the t-structure axioms simultaneously for all separated finite-type $k$-schemes by induction on their dimension. Dimensions are finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. On the empty scheme all complexes are zero, since their cohomology has no geometric fibres, by [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres], so the assertion is immediate. Let $W$ be nonempty and assume the assertion in smaller dimension. Given $A\in P^{\le0}_W$ and $B\in P^{\ge1}_W$, choose the generic open of [lem-per-qbar-generic-duality-model] for $A,B$, with reduced closed complement $Z$ of smaller dimension. Steps 2--4 and ordinary t-structure orthogonality in [def-weil-t-structure] give $\operatorname{Hom}(j^*A,j^*B)=0$; the induction hypothesis gives $\operatorname{Hom}(i^*A,i^!B)=0$. The adjunctions of [lem-per-qbar-dual-recollement] identify these with $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!j^*A,B)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(Ri_*i^*A,B)$. Its first localization triangle for $A$ therefore gives $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)=0$. The required contravariant Hom exactness is [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] applied to the dual triangle and the exact anti-equivalence of [lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality]. This proves orthogonality without assuming that the generic open has a perverse t-structure on all its constructible objects.

source.place: 1.4.10, proof of orthogonality; 2.2.10: refinement for the finitely many objects

proof.text: For $K\in\mathcal C_W$, choose a generic open as in [lem-per-qbar-generic-duality-model] for $K$, again with smaller-dimensional closed complement $Z$. On each open piece of dimension $d$, take the ordinary truncation triangle at degree $-d$; by [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres] these truncations exist in the same category and retain lisse cohomology. Assemble them as in Step 4 to obtain $A_U\to j^*K\to B_U\to A_U[1]$, with $A_U\in P^{\le0}_U$ and $B_U\in P^{\ge1}_U$. Compose $K\to Rj_*j^*K\to Rj_*B_U$ and take a fibre $K'$, using the cone axiom of [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms]. The adjunction isomorphism $j^*Rj_*\cong\operatorname{id}$ of [lem-per-qbar-dual-recollement] identifies the restriction of $K'\to K\to Rj_*B_U$ with the preceding ordinary truncation triangle, so $j^*K'\cong A_U$. On $Z$, apply the induction hypothesis to obtain $C_Z=\tau^{\ge1}_Zi^*K'$ and the corresponding lower truncation, with $C_Z\in P^{\ge1}_Z$. Form the adjunction composite $K'\to Ri_*i^*K'\to Ri_*C_Z$ and let $A$ be its fibre.

source.place: 1.4.10, proof of the truncation axiom: the two successive fibres

proof.text:
Apply the octahedral axiom [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms] to $A\to K'\to K$. If $B$ is its cone for $A\to K$, the other cone triangle is
$$Ri_*C_Z\longrightarrow B\longrightarrow Rj_*B_U\longrightarrow Ri_*C_Z[1].$$
By [lem-per-qbar-dual-recollement], $j^*Ri_*=0$ gives $j^*A\cong A_U$ and $j^*B\cong B_U$. Applying $i^*$ to $A\to K'\to Ri_*C_Z$ and using $i^*Ri_*\cong\operatorname{id}$ identifies $i^*A$ with $\tau^{\le0}_Zi^*K'$. Applying $i^!$ to the displayed triangle and using $i^!Ri_*\cong\operatorname{id}$ and $i^!Rj_*=0$ gives $i^!B\cong C_Z$. Steps 2--3 now give $A\in P^{\le0}_W$ and $B\in P^{\ge1}_W$. Thus $A\to K\to B\to A[1]$ is the required truncation triangle. Together with Steps 1 and 5, this verifies all axioms of [def-weil-t-structure], closing the induction. No compatibility of a fixed global stratification with every direct image is being assumed.

source.place: 1.4.10, octahedron and the four restriction calculations

proof.text: For boundedness, let $e=\dim W$, finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. By [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres], $\mathcal H^rK=0$ for $r>b$ for some $b$. Every remaining support has dimension at most $e$, so $\dim\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^rK\le b+e-r$ and $K\in P^{\le b+e}_W$. The dual $D_WK$ is bounded constructible by [lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality]; if its cohomology vanishes above $c$, the same argument gives $D_WK\in P^{\le c+e}_W$, hence $K\in P^{\ge-c-e}_W$. Enlarge the upper index or decrease the lower index if needed to arrange their order. The empty scheme was already treated. This proves boundedness in the sense of [def-weil-t-structure].

source.place: 2.2.17--2.2.19: bounded ordinary objects and the finite dimension range

proof.text: Fix $n$. If $K\in P^{\ge n}$, shifted orthogonality already proved gives $\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)=0$ for all $A\in P^{\le n-1}$. Conversely assume this vanishing and take the truncation triangle $A\to K\to B\to A[1]$ at $n-1$, so $A\in P^{\le n-1}$ and $B\in P^{\ge n}$. The first arrow is zero by the assumption, and $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[-1])=0$ by orthogonality, since $B[-1]\in P^{\ge n+1}\subseteq P^{\ge n}$. Exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(A,-)$ on $B[-1]\to A\to K$, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], forces $\operatorname{id}_A=0$. Thus $A=0$ and $K\cong B\in P^{\ge n}$. To see the cone map is an isomorphism, apply the same representable-Hom exactness to $0\to K\to B\to0$ for every test object, obtaining bijections on Hom; their inverses supply the inverse map. This proves exactly the displayed equivalence.
Apply [lem-sbc-tstructure-extension-closure] to the t-structure just constructed. For every $n$, both $P^{\le n}_W$ and $P^{\ge n}_W$ are closed under extensions, which is the remaining assertion.

proof_origin.place: BBD 1.4.10 two-fibre gluing proof and 4.0 support formulas, applied objectwise by dimension induction; the arbitrary-field adic structural inputs are explicitly separate nodes.

lean.statement: theorem qbar_middle_tstructure (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (X : Scheme.{u}) (Ω : Type v) [Field Ω] [Algebra (Padic l) Ω] [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω] (k : Type u) [Field k] (hl : IsUnit (l : k)) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] : ∃ t : Triangulated.TStructure (generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X), (∀ n : ℤ, t.le n = QbarPerverseLE l X Ω n) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, t.ge n = QbarPerverseGE l X Ω k hl n) ∧ (∀ K : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X, ∃ m n : ℤ, m ≤ n ∧ t.le n K ∧ t.ge m K) ∧ (∀ (n : ℤ) (K : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X), QbarPerverseGE l X Ω k hl n K ↔ ∀ A : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X, QbarPerverseLE l X Ω (n - 1) A → ∀ f : A ⟶ K, f = 0) ∧ (∀ (n : ℤ) (T : Triangle (generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X)), T ∈ distTriang (generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X) → (QbarPerverseLE l X Ω n T.obj₁ → QbarPerverseLE l X Ω n T.obj₃ → QbarPerverseLE l X Ω n T.obj₂) ∧ (QbarPerverseGE l X Ω k hl n T.obj₁ → QbarPerverseGE l X Ω k hl n T.obj₃ → QbarPerverseGE l X Ω k hl n T.obj₂))
